title: Student money basics
description: First term, first budget: the handful of money ideas every student should know.

body.heading: Know your term money
paragraphs: Student money often arrives in lumps — a loan payment, family support, a term of wages. Divide the lump by the weeks it must cover. That weekly figure is your real budget, and it is usually smaller than the lump felt.
Keep a small reserve from the start of term for end-of-term costs: travel home, course materials, and the quiet weeks before the next payment.

body.heading: Use student discounts properly
paragraphs: Student discounts are everywhere — transport, software, food, museums — but a discount on something you did not need is still spending. Ask for the discount on things already in your plan.
Check what your school offers free before paying elsewhere: printing credits, software licences, gym access, and advice services are often included in fees you have already paid.

body.heading: Ask for help early
paragraphs: If money gets tight, talk to your school's student support or advice service early. They know about hardship funds, payment plans, and local help, and asking is a normal, sensible step — not a failure.

takeaway: Divide term money by weeks, use discounts on planned buys only, and ask for help early if money gets tight.
